Analysis by Richard Cowan 

See full text of ACP report: Supporting Research into the Therapeutic Role of Marijuana 

Any statement in support of medical cannabis issued by such a large and prestigious group as the 124,000 member American College of Physicians is certain to be helpful at such a crucial time, but it is still intellectually disappointing. 

First, it is based on the 1999 Institute of Medicine Report that was itself intellectually inadequate. Now I realize that the mail may be a little slow, but it is amazing that the group would make a nine year-old review the basis of their still very timid recommendations.

See 

Executive Summary Of The IOM Report, Marijuana And Medicine: Assessing The Science Base

and the full text at 

http://www.drugsense.org/iom_report 

Second, politically the most important point is that they do come out in favor of “rescheduling” cannabis, saying, “ACP urges review of marijuana’s status as a Schedule I controlled substance and its reclassification into a more appropriate schedule, given the scientific evidence regarding marijuana’s safety and efficacy in some clinical conditions.” But even here they are lagging the principle author of the IOM report by almost four years. 

From 2004, see 

Bush’s New Freedom Initiative: “Treatment” For Using Cannabis, From The Wonderful Folks Who Brought Us Vioxx, Baycol, Etc. Author of IOM Report Says, "I can't understand why it isn't rescheduled." 

Third they strongly emphasize the need for non-smoked means of delivery, echoing the IOM report’s position, but – unlike the IOM – the ACP actually recognizes that there are other ways of using cannabis, and specifically recommending vaporization, which the IOM went to great lengths to avoid. If the IOM had been honest in 1999, this point would be obvious. 

Of course, from the moment the 1999 report was done, the Drug Czar’s office started chanting “No-medicine-is-smoked”, and have even started referring to cannabis in any vaguely medical context as “smoked marijuana.” On might get the impression that it was somehow pre-smoked, like smoked salmon. 

Third, they make a major point of saying that there should be “more research”, which is what every medical group always says, but then – in the oddest twist of all – they support “the current process for obtaining federal research-grade cannabis,” which is federal monopoly that has blocked any research that is not aimed at proving cannabis dangerous. 

Last May 31, the Los Angeles Times, which is not often mistaken for MarijuanaNews.com, ran an editorial titled “Ending the marijuana monopoly Federal officials should allow competition in growing the drug for needed studies on its medical use. ”

 

The Times observed, “Discussion of medical marijuana has always been heavy on rhetoric, elisions and grandiose claims. What it has lacked is reliable research that might bring some of the discussion into line with reality. This is because access to the government's monopoly supply of research-grade marijuana is so restricted that the necessary research is effectively impossible. Now the Drug Enforcement Administration's chief administrative law judge is recommending that the federal drug police allow competition in growing marijuana for research purposes. The administration should follow her recommendation. 

At issue is the supply of research-grade marijuana produced at the University of Mississippi and overseen by the National Institute on Drug Abuse. This supply is supposed to be made available to DEA-registered researchers who have undergone a rigorous review and approval process by the U.S. Public Health Service. However, both medical marijuana advocates and scientists say the institute routinely refuses to make its supply available even to licensed researchers for properly authorized studies. There are at least two FDA-approved studies that cannot go forward because no research samples are available….” 

Thus, it is sadly clear that even nine years after the IOM report and the bad faith manifested by the federal government, they are even lagging behind the DEA’s own Administrative Law Judge! 

The ACP still does not “get it.” 

This point is further demonstrated by their “Position 5” which says “ACP strongly supports exemption from federal criminal prosecution; civil liability; or professional sanctioning, such as loss of licensure or credentialing, for physicians who prescribe or dispense medical marijuana in accordance with state law. Similarly, ACP strongly urges protection from criminal or civil penalties for patients who use medical marijuana as permitted under state laws.”

 

Apparently, they have never heard of the Conant decision that protects from federal prosecution those doctors who discuss or even “recommend” cannabis to patients under state. 

See 

One Cheer for the American Psychiatric Association, Pending Approval of Their Call to Stop Arresting Their Medical Marijuana Patients. 

Also, they apparently don’t understand that the Feds almost never arrest and prosecute individual patients – or anyone – for possession of small cannabis. They simply do not have the resources for that. However, they certainly do prosecute patients for growing their own medicine. They certainly prosecute people who run medical cannabis dispensaries, although there is some indication that they may be having second thoughts about that. 

See 

US Attorney for Northern California Makes Nice, Maybe; LA Counterpart Talks Tough. Berkeley Better Than Oakland? One Nation Under A Bush? 

Nonetheless, they have even gone to great lengths to persecute outspoken patients like the late Robin Prosser and Steve McWilliams, both of whom were driven to suicide by federal harassment. 

See 

The Murder of Robin Prosser. An Indictment of Karen Tandy and Motorola – By Their Own Words and Standards. 

Continuing in that vein, the Czar’s “chief scientist” David Murray, said, "This is not medical science. This is a policy paper. A political act calling for political response." 

Well, it was based on a report sponsored by a previous Drug Czar, so if that is not “medical science” then whose fault is that? 

As for it being a “political act”, this is supposedly a democracy and the overwhelming majority of the American people oppose criminalizing patients, and that is a political fact, as is the opposition to medical cannabis. 

There is one more point. While the LA Times broke the story and it has been reported on television, neither the New York Times nor the Washington Post have deigned to inform their readers about it. 

NORML has had almost no calls about it, in contrast to the dozens of calls they had about the novelty of the medical marijuana vending machines in LA. 

See 

UN Says US Must Use State Violence Against Medical Marijuana Vending Machines. Threat to US Sovereignty Goes Unnoticed Because It’s “Only Marijuana.”
